name: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7
lead: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 (Pal-GQPR, sold as Rigin) is a synthetic peptide of glycine, glutamine, proline and arginine attached to palmitic acid and used in anti-aging and sensitive-skin cosmetics. [2] It is described as an anti-inflammatory signal peptide and is the second peptide in Matrixyl 3000. [2]

Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, reports it decreases IL-6 secretion in lab models. [2] Peptides in general are widely used in sensitive-skin products, according to an analysis of 88 facial cosmetics. [3] Published human efficacy data specific to this peptide are limited.

paras: The palmitoyl group raises lipophilicity to aid passage through the stratum corneum. [2] It appears in multi-peptide formulations; US labels list it with other peptides in stretch mark creams. [6]

Reported laboratory effects include lowering IL-6 after stressors such as UVB, and promoting basement membrane proteins. [2] A study of dermal extracellular matrix and the epidermal-dermal junction examined effects of age and peptide applications using imaging methods. [4]
A 2026 study applied serums with both Matrixyl 3000 peptides to three volunteers and detected both in stratum corneum layers with signal decreasing with depth. [1]

A study of a multi-component eye cream containing palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 alongside other actives evaluated efficacy and safety in the periorbital area, so effects cannot be assigned to one ingredient. [5] No trial of this peptide alone was found.

card.summary: The anti-inflammatory peptide half of Matrixyl 3000; present in many serums, with little isolated human data.
card.note: Mechanism claims come largely from lab data and an AI-generated reference.

quick.overview:
Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 is a lab-made peptide with a fatty acid tail, used in anti-aging and sensitive-skin products. It is paired with palmitoyl tripeptide-1 in Matrixyl 3000.

Its effects in people have mostly been studied inside multi-ingredient products, not on its own.
quick.mechanism: In lab models it is reported to reduce inflammatory IL-6 release and to support skin matrix proteins.
quick.risks: Sold as a cosmetic ingredient; labels advise external use only and avoiding the eyes. No ingredient-specific safety data were found.
